agent_output.affected_group: Handlers (and growers/importers) of walnuts grown in California subject to Federal Marketing Order No. 984 (7 CFR part 984), including handlers receiving imported walnuts
agent_output.change_summary: USDA/AMS announced a public hearing (April 19-20, 2022, remote via Zoom) on California Walnut Board-recommended amendments to Marketing Order No. 984 that would eliminate mandatory inspection and certification of outbound inshell/shelled walnuts (and imported walnuts), remove volume control authority, change handler assessments from kernelweight on shipped walnuts to inshell pound on received walnuts with a proposed initial rate of $0.0125 per inshell pound, and add authority to charge late payment/interest. This is a notification of hearing, the first step in formal rulemaking; amendments require later recommended decision, Secretary's decision and grower referendum before implementation.

evidence.quote: ACTION: Notification of hearing on proposed rulemaking.

USDA will oversee this formal rulemaking proceeding. The issuance 
of this notification of public hearing is the first of several steps in 
the amendatory rulemaking process, including the issuance of a 
recommended decision, public comment period, Secretary's decision, 
grower referendum, and handler sign-up (if the prior steps prove 
favorable).

Finally, any proposed amendments must be approved 
in a grower referendum before they can be implemented.

The California 
Walnut Board (Board), which locally administers the Order, recommended 
proposed amendments that would eliminate mandatory inspection and 
certification of inshelled and shelled walnuts, and of shelled walnuts 
for processing; create a new mechanism for determining and collecting 
handler assessments; add authority to charge interest for late 
payments; and remove volume control authority.

As proposed, inspection and 
certification of outbound walnuts would no longer be required, and 
handler assessments would be calculated based on a proposed assessment 
rate recommended by the Board and applied to handlers' inbound walnuts 
instead of outbound walnuts.

The Board has proposed an initial assessment rate of 
$0.0125 per inshell pound of walnuts that would go into effect with the 
start of the proposed new mechanism, if it were to be effectuated.

DATES: The hearing will be held April 19-20, 2022, from 8:00 a.m. to 
5:00 p.m. Pacific Time (PT)

Notice is hereby given of a public hearing to receive evidence 
on proposed amendments to Federal Marketing Order No. 984 (Order) 
regulating the handling of walnuts grown in California.

If implemented, the Board states the proposed amendments would remove 
the redundancy of the outbound inspection, thus reducing costs to both 
handlers and producers and reducing administrative burden to the Board. 
Accordingly, inspection and certification requirements for imported 
walnuts would also be removed.

The Board also requested the current moratorium on enforcement 
of mandatory inspection requirements be extended until the effective 
date of the proposed amendments summarized in this notification, if 
approved.

uncertainties: No effective date; only hearing dates (April 19-20, 2022) and pre-registration deadline (April 12, 2022).
Proposed only; implementation depends on later steps and grower referendum; not assessed.
Internal inconsistency: narrative says $0.0125 per inshell pound while proposed regulatory text for Sec. 984.347 reads $0.125; flagged, not resolved.
event_type is a judgment call; could be price_or_terms_change.
Prior indefinite suspension of volume control (June 8, 2020, 85 FR 27107) and an existing moratorium on inspection enforcement mean some removals may already be non-enforced.
